subject: Connors Scholarship and Technology Infrastructure Upgrades
overview: The committee authorized an application for federal technology infrastructure funding and reviewed reports on college acceptances, a new $4 million scholarship fund, and opioid prevention initiatives. Discussion also addressed maintenance priorities and the projected impact of the FY18 state budget on local school aid.

items.title: Minutes and Financial Approvals
items.summary: Approved amended minutes from April 3rd, minutes from April 24th, bills, transfers, and payrolls.

items.title: Connors Scholarship Program Report
items.summary: The Director of Guidance reported that a $4 million investment by James and Thelma Connors will provide scholarships of up to $33,000 for Medford students, with approximately 60 applications expected.

items.title: Class of 2017 College Acceptances
items.summary: Staff presented preliminary data showing 220 students accepted to over 225 institutions, including several Ivy League universities and local partnerships like Tufts University.

items.title: Youth Opioid Prevention Grant
items.summary: The district was awarded $18,000 from an Attorney General settlement to fund health education kits for elementary schools, faculty training, and parent education forums.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and School Choice
items.summary: Approved the 2017-2018 meeting schedule and voted to reject participation in the state's school choice program for the upcoming academic year.

items.title: Technology Infrastructure Study and E-Rate Funding
items.summary: The committee authorized the administration to apply for $398,100 in federal E-rate funding for network upgrades requiring a $265,400 local match, while tabling the full infrastructure report for vendor clarification.

items.title: Buildings and Grounds Pre-Budget Report
items.summary: John McLaughlin detailed maintenance needs across 1.2 million square feet of facilities, including high school door replacements and flooring repairs, supported by a proposed $200,000 increase in the repair budget.

items.title: FY18 State Budget Report
items.summary: Superintendent Belson warned of limited state aid increases and potential funding gaps in special education, charter school reimbursements, and homeless transportation.

items.title: Resolutions and Condolences
items.summary: Passed condolence resolutions for Irene Hagee, mother of a former administrative assistant, and Ahmed Azizi, a former custodian.
